clips.text: A volcano is a mountain with a very hot secret.
Deep under the ground, it is so hot that rock melts. Melted rock is called magma.
Magma is full of gas. It pushes up, harder and harder, like the fizz in a bottle of lemonade that you've shaken.
Then, whoosh. Out it comes, through the top. Once it's outside, we call it lava.
The lava cools down, and turns back into hard rock. So every time it erupts, the mountain grows a little taller.
So remember. Inside the volcano, it's magma. Outside, it's lava. And now you know more than most grown-ups.
